title: For an abelian etale sheaf on Spec K whose geometric stalk identifies equivariantly with a discrete Galois representation M, its sheaf cohomology in every degree is equivalent to continuous cohomology of M.
statement: The adopted source construction gives the canonical additive comparison between etale sheaf cohomology on Spec K and continuous cohomology of a discrete Gal(Ks/K)-module. Its precise Lean signature is the existing declaration `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.sheafHAddEquivContinuousCohomology`: noncomputable def sheafHAddEquivContinuousCohomology (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (M : TopRep.{u} ℤ Gal(Ks/K)) [DiscreteTopology M.V] (c : ((galoisPoint K Ks).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj F ≃+ M.V) (hc : ∀ (σ : Gal(Ks/K)) (v : ((galoisPoint K Ks).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj F), c ((galoisPoint K Ks).presheafFiberAct (galoisPointAct K Ks) F.obj σ v) = M.ρ σ (c v)) (n : ℕ) : Sheaf.H F n ≃+ continuousCohomology n M.

proof.text: Compare etale cohomology of F on Spec K with Ext from the integers in discrete Gal(Ks/K)-modules of the stalk at the Galois point, via the equivalence of etale sheaves on Spec K with discrete Galois modules (Tag 04JQ) under which global sections are invariants (Tag 03QU): the source comparison `sheafHAddEquivGaloisH`.

Compute that Ext by homogeneous continuous cochains (Section 0DVG), transporting the coefficients along the equivariant additive equivalence c (hypothesis hc): the source comparison `DiscreteModule.hAddEquivContinuousCohomology`. The composite is the additive equivalence of the statement.

statement_change.what: The retired Sheaf theorem used an arbitrary algebraic closure Ω, an explicit action-on-germs condition, and a Nonempty equivalence. The adopted source module instead provides the canonical additive comparison at the Galois point; the duplicate theorem and its module are withdrawn, and the sole consumer uses this source declaration directly.

old_proof.text: Obtain the abelian geometric stalk equivalence E, its underlying additive stalk comparison i, and its action-on-germs formula. Choose the identity etale terminal object T and evaluation V at T.
Identify V naturally with invariants of E by the degree-zero global sections lemma. Compose i_F with c to obtain an additive equivalence d from E(F) to M.

Prove d is equivariant: extend g to an automorphism tau of Omega, represent i_F(z) by a germ using joint surjectivity, and form the transported geometric lift xprime by Spec(tau). The canonical action formula and hc identify both sides. Apply i_F inverse to the germ identity to recover z.

Form the natural isomorphism from evaluation V to invariants using the additive equivalences t and ht. Convert d to its canonical integer-linear equivalence and apply the existing discrete-invariants continuous comparison. This gives an equivalence from right-derived evaluation to homogeneous continuous cohomology of M, with no finite-ring hypothesis.

For positive degrees, identify Sheaf.H with right-derived evaluation using the existing injective-resolution comparison. In degree zero, compose Sheaf.H.equiv0 with the inverse of rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. Compose the additive equivalences and forget additivity to obtain the required Nonempty equivalence.
